chapter: Reading bands, brass bands and Fate Marable
title: Jake Chambers's brass band and Joe Johnson
summary: Williams names the men in Chambers's reading brass band and recalls Joe Johnson as a thin, fine trumpeter.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: What about those other brass bands now? No. No, no, no, those other brass bands at that time. I was wondering about them.
Jake Chambers, he had a brass band too, you know.

No. Mud Carey would play him and Mud Carey and Joe Johnson, the trumpet player, you know. Joe Johnson, Ernest Kelly on trombone. But they could read. See, little Joe Johnson could read. Ernest Kelly too. Ernest Kelly, Joe Johnson, Mud Carey, Tate Chambers, sometimes Bunk Johnson, the trumpet.
You remember Bunk back then, right?
I remember my little, I remember my singing playing blues with Tate Chambers.
Did Tate have a name for that band? Columbia. Should be the Columbia Brass.
Brass band and his orchestra too.
And what about Joe Johnson? What was he like?

That's a guy I don't know anything about. He was a little thin fellow. He was a little thin fellow like he had TB. I think that's what he died with. Fine trumpet player. Yeah, fine trumpet. Brown trumpet felt thin, very thin. Oh, he drank himself to death. What did he play like?
Did he play like anybody you knew?
No, well at that time, you know, I was young, you know. See how, yeah, I didn't. But I know he was a nice trumpet player.
